rows: Maintain accounting records, systems, and financial reports

Mercor Loop Harness with Claude Fable 5 (Max), $50 task budget and accounting-system/file tools; APEX-Accounting v1 evaluation on 160 expert-authored month-end-close and bookkeeping tasks across 10 simulated companies

Evidence grade A; research-only benchmark. The coherent agent worked across an accounting system, spreadsheets, PDFs, and other files to reconcile accounts, accrue expenses, post transactions, and produce reports. Claude Fable 5 led at 56.4% Mean Criteria@3, but the most consistent model solved only 2.6% of tasks correctly in all eight runs, and 58% of tasks were never fully solved by any model. Direct execution establishes substantial contribution to Acquire, Interpret, Decide, and Act, but reasoning, information-gathering, instruction-following, and planning failures still require routine substantive human completion. Protocol 0.4 permits a bounded frontier ceiling, but this representative 160-task evaluation does not identify a stage-complete autonomous subset with acceptable repeated performance; therefore 2/2/2/2. Scope is month-end close and bookkeeping; tax, audit, consolidation, multi-entity or multi-currency accounting, and external reporting were not evaluated.

Conduct and report audit or assurance engagements

MindBridge Platform continuous-release General Ledger audit configuration (documentation through 2026-07-20): Audit Assertion Risk, automated scoping, risk-stratified sampling/Audit Plan, and report exports

Evidence grade C; commercial system. Humans request, load or connect, and validate and reconcile the engagement data, while MindBridge contributes bounded ingestion and completeness functions (Acquire 1). Its rules, statistics, and machine-learning ensemble analyzes the ledger, assigns assertion and account risk, surfaces anomalous entries, and supports investigation (Interpret 2). It automatically scopes quantitatively material balances from human-set materiality and generates risk-stratified samples and tasks, but auditors make qualitative scope, procedure, significance, and conclusion judgments (Decide 2). It generates planning, account, Audit Plan, and documentation exports, while humans perform broader examination and issue the assurance report (Act 2). Public documentation provides no representative performance or override rates and requires skilled interpretation and firm oversight, so no stage can reach 3.

Provide financial planning, analysis, and decision support
OpenAI ChatGPT product agent using GPT-5.1 in Pro mode, external web browsing enabled, historical chats disabled; Finch/FinWorkBench 172-workflow configuration (2026-04-15)

Evidence grade A. Across 172 authentic, messy enterprise workflows, the coherent product agent browsed the web, retrieved and parsed supplied files, calculated and validated models and scenarios, and generated or modified workbooks, charts, and reports. This supports Acquire 2, Interpret 2, and Act 2. Benchmark instructions usually specified assumptions and transformations; they demonstrated decision cues, not independent selection of defensible assumptions, budgets, or management recommendations, so Decide is 1. Human gold evaluation passed 66/172 workflows (38.4%), falling to 23.5% for workflows with more than two tasks and 35% for multimodal workflows; retrieval, formula, business-logic, and rendering failures require substantive correction. No stage reaches 3. A separate MBABench profile has stronger Decide but weaker Acquire and is retained as a crossed candidate; this row is unresolved rather than combined.

Determine and document tax liabilities and filings

Invaro OpenTax MCP (public repository and methodology accessed 2026-08-19; exact release or commit not reported) with an Anthropic Claude Sonnet agent (exact model/version and harness not reported), one cold attempt per TaxCalcBench TY2025 case; 50 constructed federal-and-state return cases

Evidence grade B for the open engine and disclosed benchmark methodology, with material configuration and run-provenance gaps. Claude transcribed benchmark-supplied taxpayer PDFs and companion case facts into OpenTax inputs, a substantial but incomplete acquisition contribution because the benchmark supplied a curated, complete case folder and did not test locating records or identifying missing documents (Acquire 2). The reported configuration applied encoded and cited rules and scored 48/50 cases exact and 805/820 scored lines in one cold pass per case. However, the exact Claude model/version, OpenTax release or commit, prompts, tool traces, saved outputs, and repeat-run reliability were not published, so the evidence cannot distinguish 3 from 4 for Interpret or Decide; both are IE rather than arbitrarily downgraded. The system produced calculated line sets and proof output but not a complete filing package, all required forms and schedules, MeF-compatible output, submission, signatures, or payment execution (Act 2). Commercial availability and deployment scale do not affect these scores.

Deliver and sustain a software system or change

OpenAI internal Codex agent harness used for agent-first product development (Aug 2025–Feb 2026; GPT-5-series model version not fully disclosed), with repository tools, issue/PR workflow, isolated worktrees, browser, logs/metrics, tests/CI, agent review, and merge permission

Evidence grade B; detailed operational developer deployment, with the exact evolving model version incompletely disclosed. OpenAI's coherent Codex harness built and shipped an internal product whose application code, tests, CI, documentation, observability, and tooling were agent-generated (about 1 million lines and 1,500 merged pull requests). From a single prompt, agents gathered repository and runtime context, reproduced a bug, selected and implemented a fix, validated the application, handled feedback and build failures, and merged; human pull-request review was optional and escalation occurred only when judgment was required. Under Protocol 0.4's frontier-ceiling rule, this directly supports Acquire/Interpret/Decide/Act = 4/4/4/4 for a substantive, agent-legible software-development configuration. Human goal-setting and reusable harness engineering do not lower the rating. The configuration depends on encoded requirements and architecture, isolated worktrees, browser/log/metric access, executable tests and CI, agent review, and merge authority; the 4s do not mean universal coverage of every software setting. Current Claude Fable 5 in Claude Code provides corroborating long-horizon evidence but is not combined into this coherent profile.

Evaluate patients through diagnostic imaging and communicate findings

Oxipit ChestLink v2.6 configured for autonomous high-confidence-normal reporting of eligible adult posteroanterior chest radiographs (frontal with optional lateral), with automatic PACS/RIS workflow integration

Evidence grade A for external diagnostic performance plus manufacturer IFU for autonomous workflow. In a consecutive four-hospital cohort of 1,529 examinations, ChestLink achieved 99.1% sensitivity for any abnormality and 99.8% for critical abnormality while selecting 120 of 429 normal studies (7.8% of all examinations) for autonomous reporting. For the bounded eligible-PA-CXR configuration, it automatically receives and eligibility-checks DICOM, interprets normality, commits the normal-versus-route decision, and sends a final structured report to PACS/RIS without radiologist interpretation; periodic sampled quality audit is after the fact. Under Protocol 0.4, this supports 4/4/4/4. An upstream technologist still creates the image, but that is outside the radiologist-side acquisition stage. The system excludes AP views, does not compare priors or gather broader history, explains no finding, and routes abnormal or uncertain cases to a radiologist; the 4s are a frontier ceiling for this narrow but substantive configuration, not broad radiology coverage.

Plan and perform image-guided procedures and manage procedural care

Mohan–Agrawal–Patel autonomous impedance-controlled ultrasound-guided percutaneous needle-placement system, configured for liver-region localization, robotic scanning, target localization, trajectory planning, and needle insertion/retrieval in agar phantoms

Evidence grade B; research-only controlled test. In the demonstrated static agar-phantom configuration, the integrated prototype autonomously localized the liver region, acquired an ultrasound volume, localized targets, planned insertion angle and depth, and inserted and retrieved the needle without human intervention. Impedance control completed all 30/30 target attempts with 5.74 ± 2.70 mm mean targeting error and 26.71 seconds mean targeting time. This supports 4/4/4/4 for that bounded laboratory workflow. It does not establish autonomous clinical biopsy or broader procedural-care capability: there was no patient or animal use, tissue sampling, breathing or organ motion, sterility, anesthesia, physiologic monitoring, bleeding or complication management, counseling, or documentation.
